content: 1. Encorafenib can both inhibit and induce the metabolism of CYP3A4 enzymes at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. This dual effect necessitates caution and close monitoring when co-administered with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, as it may lead to increased toxicity or reduced efficacy of these agents. 2. Atazanavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting its metabolism through hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Enfortumab vedotin, an antibody-drug conjugate, releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage, and MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 in vitro. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as cobicistat, may increase MMAE exposure, heightening the risk of enfortumab vedotin-related toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Atazanavir and enfuvirtide both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Careful monitoring is recommended during their use. 4. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary when these drugs are used together. 5. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the erlotinib dose in 50 mg increments and monitor for adverse effects. 6. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate forms) increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 7. Atazanavir increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Atazanavir enhances the effects of esmolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, atrioventricular block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose and monitor closely. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Atazanavir may increase or decrease estradiol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised, and alternatives should be considered if available. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal formulations by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with estrogens may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Atazanavir may increase or decrease levels of conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, or estropipate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised, and alternatives should be considered if available. 14. Atazanavir increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day and monitor closely. 15. Atazanavir increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. 16. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel, etoposide, and etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 17. Atazanavir may increase or decrease etynodiol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised, and alternatives should be considered if available. 18. Atazanavir decreases the effects of exenatide (injectable solution or suspension) due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors, potentially causing hyperglycemia. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir and cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary and monitor closely. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of felodipine and fentanyl (including intranasal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 21. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of felodipine, fentanyl, fesoterodine, and fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 22. Cobicistat increases fluoxetine levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor response during co-administration. 23. Atazanavir increases flurazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised, and alternatives should be considered if available. 24. Cobicistat increases fluticasone levels (both furoate and inhaled forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Cobicistat increases fluvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Start with the lowest recommended dose of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and titrate while monitoring for safety. 26. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir and fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both atazanavir and fosamprenavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Fluvoxamine increases cobicistat levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor response during co-administration. 28. Cobicistat increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing exposure to its active metabolite R406. Monitor for toxicities and adjust the fostamatinib dose as needed. 29. Garlic decreases atazanavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 31. Atazanavir and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. If co-administered, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 33. Atazanavir decreases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors, potentially causing hyperglycemia. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Atazanavir increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 35. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 36. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely and adjust hydrocodone doses as needed. 37. Atazanavir increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Cobicistat decreases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting its metabolism to active alkylating metabolites, potentially reducing its efficacy. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 39. Atazanavir increases hydroxprogesterone caproate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 40. Atazanavir decreases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting its metabolism to active alkylating metabolites, potentially reducing its efficacy. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 41. Atazanavir increases iloperidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while iloperidone increases atazanavir levels as a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
